title: OL 8 must disable the systemd Ctrl-Alt-Delete burst key sequence.
check_content:
Verify OL 8 is not configured to reboot the system when Ctrl-Alt-Delete is pressed seven times within two seconds with the following command: 
 
$ sudo grep -i ctrl /etc/systemd/system.conf 
 
CtrlAltDelBurstAction=none 
 
If the "CtrlAltDelBurstAction" is not set to "none" or is commented out or missing, this is a finding.
fixtext:
Configure the system to disable the CtrlAltDelBurstAction by added or modifying the following line in the "/etc/systemd/system.conf" configuration file: 
 
CtrlAltDelBurstAction=none 
 
Reload the daemon for this change to take effect: 
 
$ sudo systemctl daemon-reload
VulnDiscussion: A locally logged-on user who presses Ctrl-Alt-Delete when at the console can reboot the system. If accidentally pressed, as could happen in the case of a mixed OS environment, this can create the risk of short-term loss of availability of systems due to unintentional reboot. In a graphical user environment, risk of unintentional reboot from the Ctrl-Alt-Delete sequence is reduced because the user will be prompted before any action is taken.
